# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 3

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

I have no tactile information yet: the display, light, and all three wire markings are unknown to me. I’m asking Mute to use gestures to relay the manual’s rule through Deaf, while Deaf should verbally report every visible marking and colour so I can combine both sources before cutting anything.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="I feel no markings or clues. Please use gestures to relay the manual's rule to Deaf. Have Deaf report the full visual display, light, and wire markings aloud to me. Use finger signs for wire positions: ☝ means 1, ✌ means 2, 🤟 means 3.")
```

(empty)

No new information has arrived. I should not cut an unknown wire. My earlier request still needs to be carried through the speaking order, so I will wait for the Deaf monkey’s report.

```text
wait()
```

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Please gesture 👍 to Deaf to request a complete report of the display, light, and all wire markings. Then tell me the manual's rule and Deaf's report in your next speaking turn.")
```

Deaf has reported the visible state: display 0; light sequence blue, orange, yellow; wire colours 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 blue. I cannot determine the correct cut from that alone because I do not have the manual. I’m sending Mute the complete state and asking for the manual’s prescribed wire position.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Deaf reports display 0; light sequence blue, orange, yellow; wire 1 red, wire 2 yellow, wire 3 blue. Which wire position does the manual prescribe?")
```

The new red light does not resolve the manual rule. Deaf’s report confirms the same wire colours, but the gesture from Mute is invisible to me and therefore carries no usable content. I still need Mute’s manual-based answer, so I will ask again for the exact wire position and avoid acting.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="I cannot perceive gestures. Please speak the manual's prescribed wire position for display 0, light sequence blue-orange-yellow-red, and wires red/yellow/blue.")
```

The visible state is now display 0, light sequence blue–orange–yellow–red–green, with wires 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 blue. I still lack the manual’s rule and therefore cannot safely choose a wire. I’ll request the exact answer from Mute once more.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Please answer directly with the safe wire position, 1, 2, or 3, using the current state: display 0; lights blue, orange, yellow, red, green; wires red, yellow, blue.")
```

The correct communication path is Mute’s gesture to Deaf, followed by Deaf’s spoken report to me; Mute cannot speak directly. Deaf confirms receiving a gesture but has not identified it, so I’m asking Mute to use the agreed one-symbol wire code and asking Deaf to report which gesture was seen. I will not cut until that position is relayed.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Gesture the manual's wire position to Deaf now: ☝ means wire 1, ✌ means wire 2, 🤟 means wire 3. Deaf, please identify and report the gesture you receive.")
```

The bomb’s visible state continues to change, but no safe wire rule has been relayed. Since Mute cannot speak, the needed path is Mute’s gesture to Deaf and Deaf’s spoken identification to me. I’m asking Deaf to report the exact gesture, not merely the bomb state.

```text
speak(to="deaf", text="Did Mute gesture a wire position? Please report the exact gesture or describe its hand shape, then state whether it means wire 1, 2, or 3.")
```

System: Nobody could receive that, so your speak reached nobody.
Deaf says to Blind: Update: display 0; light is yellow. The observed repeating light sequence is blue, orange, yellow, red, green. Wires unchanged: 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 blue.

My last message to Deaf was useless because Deaf cannot hear speech. The only viable route for the manual is Mute’s gesture to Deaf, followed by Deaf’s spoken report to me. I will explicitly request that Mute make the wire-position gesture on the next Mute turn, and I will continue waiting rather than risk a cut.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="On your next turn, gesture exactly one wire choice to Deaf: ☝ for wire 1, ✌ for wire 2, or 🤟 for wire 3. Deaf will report which gesture you made.")
```

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Update: display 0; light is red. The observed repeating light sequence is blue, orange, yellow, red, green. Wires unchanged: 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 blue.

The light is merely cycling through the known sequence and does not identify a wire. I still have no manual instruction, and cutting any of the three wires would be a guess. Since Mute can see my gestures, I’ll reinforce the request for Mute to relay the manual’s choice to Deaf using the agreed position signs.

```text
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["🙏", "☝", "✌", "🤟"])
wait()
```

ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Update: display 0; light is green. Repeating sequence is blue, orange, yellow, red, green. Wires unchanged: 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 blue. Mute signalled the V-shaped hand gesture ? again; its meaning is unknown.

The V-shaped gesture is ✌, which matches the agreed code for wire 2. Mute has therefore relayed wire position 2 through Deaf, even though Deaf cannot know its meaning independently. I will cut wire 2.

```text
act(op="cut", position=2)
```
